newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sets $16.50/barrel oil price in budget.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sets $16.50/barrel oil price in budget.

text.p: Indonesia has set its oil price at $16.50 per barrel in its 1997/98 (April-March) budget, unchanged from the current budget, Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said.

"The 1997/98 budget sets the oil price at $16.50 per barrel. Oil production is 1.520 million barrels per day (bpd), including 190,000 barrels of condensate per day," he told a briefing ahead of President Suharto's budget speech to parliament on Monday.
Mar'ie said the government projected revenue from crude oil at 10.69 trillion rupiah in 1997/98, up from 10.32 trillion rupiah in 1996/97.
He said revenue from gas was expected to be 4.18 trillion rupiah in 1997/98, up from 3.80 trillion rupiah in 1996/97.
He said total revenue from oil would account for 16.9 percent of overall budgeted income in 1997/98, compared with 18.1 percent in the 1996/97 budget.
Non-oil revenue would rise to 83.1 percent in 1997/98 from 81.9 percent in the current budget.
"Total revenue from oil and gas will only increase by 5.3 percent in 1997/98 from the current budget. This is good because we will continue to reduce our dependency on oil," Mar'ie said.
A budget report released by government said the average Indonesian oil price eased in November to $22.47 per barrel from $23.04 per barrel in October.

"It is estimated in the 1997/98 budget that oil supply in the international market will increase, especially because of the oil-for-food deal with Iraq and because production from non-OPEC countries can not be controlled," the report said.
